stem: The digestion of starch begins in the mouth due to the action of which enzyme present in saliva?
explanation: Salivary amylase begins breaking down starch into simpler sugars right in the mouth — pepsin (stomach) digests proteins, and trypsin/lipase (small intestine, from pancreatic secretions) digest proteins and fats respectively.
